title: PwC's US CEO built an AI assistant called 'PG's Whisperer.' He talks to it all day.
excerpt: PwC's US CEO Paul Griggs said he built the same custom AI assistant on two models and keeps them pulled up all day.
content_html:
Leaders don't just want their employees using AI — they're taking advantage of the tech, too.

PwC senior partner and US CEO Paul Griggs is embracing that challenge as he says the company experiences its strongest pipeline of new clients.

The Big Four leader told Business Insider that he "got nudged" to experiment with AI more and now keeps two chat systems open on his phone and computer throughout the day. He declined to name which models he uses, but said his go-to tool is a custom AI model he dubbed "PG's Whisperer," which he created using two different models.

"I use PG's Whisperer all day long, and then I contrast and compare information," Griggs said.

Griggs said PG's Whisperer has been around for about a year, and he's become a big fan. The tool emerged from conversations with a PwC colleague who works on the firm's intelligent enterprise offerings.

After the two spent time "pinging back and forth," the colleague encouraged Griggs to build a customized solution rather than relying solely on prompting to get the results he wanted. Griggs said the colleague gave him the steps to build it over text.

"That, to me, was an acceleration of my own discovery," Griggs said.

Mastering AI isn't the only new demand facing consulting executives. The rapid pace of business, as well as the pressure to stay ahead of clients, is raising the stakes for leaders.

Griggs said he uses AI to review lengthy documents, test ideas against what he's seen in the news, and pressure-test strategy work. It allows him to assess information at a speed that was "simply not possible before," he said.

He also feeds the assistant material he plans to say or do, including speeches he's writing, and asks for feedback. Sometimes, his question is as straightforward as: "Does it suck or does it not?" he said. Other times, he asks whether the point he's trying to make is actually coming through — and what he should change if it isn't.

"I don't know what my token consumption is, but I can tell you that somebody does, and it would be significant," Griggs said.

sentences.zh: 领导

content_html_zh:
领导者不仅希望他们的员工使用人工智能——他们也正在利用这项技术。

普华永道高级合伙人兼美国首席执行官保罗·格里格斯（Paul Griggs）正在迎接这一挑战，他表示公司正经历着最强劲的新客户渠道。

这位四大巨头的领导人告诉《商业内幕》，他“受到推动”更多地尝试人工智能，现在他的手机和电脑上的两个聊天系统全天保持打开状态。 他拒绝透露自己使用的模型，但表示他的首选工具是一个定制的人工智能模型，他称之为“PG's Whisperer”，他使用两种不同的模型创建了该模型。

“我整天使用 PG 的 Whisperer，然后对比和比较信息，”格里格斯说。

Griggs 表示 PG 的 Whisperer 已经推出大约一年了，他已经成为了它的忠实粉丝。 该工具是在与普华永道一位从事该公司智能企业产品工作的同事的对话中诞生的。

在两人花时间“来回沟通”后，这位同事鼓励格里格斯构建一个定制的解决方案，而不是仅仅依靠提示来获得他想要的结果。 格里格斯说，这位同事向他提供了通过文本构建它的步骤。

“对我来说，这加速了我自己的发现，”格里格斯说。

掌握人工智能并不是咨询高管面临的唯一新需求。 业务的快速发展以及保持领先于客户的压力正在提高领导者的风险。

格里格斯说，他使用人工智能来审查冗长的文档，根据他在新闻中看到的内容来测试想法，并对策略工作进行压力测试。 他说，这使他能够以“以前根本不可能”的速度评估信息。

他还向助理提供他计划说或做的材料，包括他正在写的演讲，并寻求反馈。 有时，他的问题很简单：“这很糟糕吗？” 他说。 其他时候，他会问他试图表达的观点是否真正得到实现——如果没有实现，他应该改变什么。

格里格斯说：“我不知道我的代币消费量是多少，但我可以告诉你有人知道，而且这会很重要。”
